facts.f: At sea level, water boils at 100 °C and freezes at 0 °C.
facts.e: The Celsius scale was built around these two points.

facts.f: A water molecule is made of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom: H2O.
facts.e: That is why water's chemical formula is H2O.

facts.f: Isaac Newton described the laws of motion and the law of gravity.
facts.e: He published them in his famous book, the Principia, in 1687.

facts.f: Without air, a feather and a hammer fall at the same speed.
facts.e: Astronaut David Scott showed this on the Moon in 1971, where there is no air to slow the feather.

facts.f: In empty space, light travels at about 3 lakh km every second.
facts.e: Nothing travels faster than light.

facts.f: Sound travels faster in water than in air, and fastest in solids.
facts.e: The particles in solids are packed closely, so they pass the vibrations along quickly.

facts.f: Thomas Edison developed a practical, long-lasting electric light bulb in 1879.
facts.e: Others had made bulbs before, but his lasted long enough to be useful in homes.

facts.f: Alexander Graham Bell received the first patent for the telephone in 1876.
facts.e: The first words he spoke on it were to his assistant, Thomas Watson.

facts.f: The Wright brothers made the first powered, controlled aeroplane flight in 1903.
facts.e: Orville Wright's first flight lasted only 12 seconds.

facts.f: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin, the first antibiotic, in 1928.
facts.e: He noticed that a mould had killed bacteria growing in a dish.

facts.f: Marie Curie was the first person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences.
facts.e: She won in Physics in 1903 and in Chemistry in 1911.

facts.f: C. V. Raman won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930.
facts.e: He was the first Asian to win a Nobel Prize in science, for discovering the Raman effect in how light scatters.

facts.f: India celebrates National Science Day on 28 February.
facts.e: It marks C. V. Raman's discovery of the Raman effect in 1928.

facts.f: Dmitri Mendeleev arranged the elements into a periodic table in 1869.
facts.e: He even left gaps for elements that had not been discovered yet, and predicted what they would be like.

facts.f: An atom has a centre called the nucleus, with electrons moving around it.
facts.e: The nucleus contains protons and neutrons.

facts.f: With magnets, like poles repel and unlike poles attract.
facts.e: Two north poles push apart, but a north and a south pole pull together.

facts.f: An object in water is pushed up by a force equal to the weight of water it pushes aside.
facts.e: This is Archimedes' principle. It explains why ships float.

facts.f: Johannes Gutenberg built a printing press with movable metal type in the mid-1400s.
facts.e: It made books much cheaper and faster to produce.

facts.f: In 628 CE, the Indian mathematician Brahmagupta wrote rules for calculating with zero.
facts.e: He explained, for example, that a number minus itself is zero.

facts.f: The place-value system of numbers we use today was developed in India.
facts.e: It spread to the world through Arab scholars, so the digits are often called Hindu-Arabic numerals.

facts.f: Aryabhata, born in 476 CE, explained that Earth spins on its axis.
facts.e: He wrote this in his book, the Aryabhatiya, about 1,500 years ago.

facts.f: Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction in 1831.
facts.e: Moving a magnet near a wire makes electricity flow. Power station generators work this way.

facts.f: Steel is made mostly of iron with a little carbon.
facts.e: The carbon makes it much stronger than pure iron.

facts.f: Mixing blue and yellow paint makes green.
facts.e: Blue, yellow and red paints can be mixed to make many other colours.

facts.f: White light is a mix of all the colours of the rainbow.
facts.e: Isaac Newton showed this by splitting sunlight with a glass prism.

facts.f: Plants grow towards light.
facts.e: This is called phototropism. It helps leaves catch more sunlight.

facts.f: Rust forms when iron reacts with oxygen and water.
facts.e: Painting or oiling iron keeps air and water away and stops rust.

facts.f: There are six simple machines: lever, pulley, wheel and axle, inclined plane, wedge and screw.
facts.e: Simple machines make work easier. A see-saw is a lever.

facts.f: Friction is a force that slows moving things down.
facts.e: Rough surfaces make more friction. Smooth, wet or icy surfaces make less, which is why they are slippery.

facts.f: Louis Pasteur showed that germs cause many diseases.
facts.e: Pasteurisation, heating milk to kill germs, is named after him.

facts.f: Wilhelm Röntgen discovered X-rays in 1895.
facts.e: X-rays pass through skin but not easily through bone, so doctors can see inside the body.

facts.f: Charles Darwin explained evolution by natural selection in his book On the Origin of Species, in 1859.
facts.e: Living things that suit their surroundings best tend to survive and pass on their features.

facts.f: Albert Einstein's famous equation E = mc² shows that mass and energy are linked.
facts.e: A tiny amount of mass can turn into a huge amount of energy.

facts.f: Homi J. Bhabha is called the father of India's nuclear programme.
facts.e: He founded the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and led India's atomic energy work.

facts.f: Vikram Sarabhai is called the father of the Indian space programme.
facts.e: He helped set up ISRO and India's first rocket launching station at Thumba, Kerala.

facts.f: Jagadish Chandra Bose showed that plants respond to their surroundings.
facts.e: He invented the crescograph, an instrument that measures very tiny amounts of plant growth.

facts.f: Srinivasa Ramanujan was a self-taught mathematical genius from Tamil Nadu.
facts.e: India celebrates National Mathematics Day on his birthday, 22 December.

facts.f: Lemon juice and vinegar taste sour because they contain acids.
facts.e: Never taste chemicals to test them. Scientists use indicators like litmus paper instead.

facts.f: Ice, water and steam are the same substance in three different states.
facts.e: Solid, liquid and gas. Heating or cooling changes one state into another.

facts.f: A magnifying glass is a convex lens.
facts.e: A convex lens is thicker in the middle. It bends light to make things look bigger.

facts.f: Galileo was one of the first people to study the sky with a telescope.
facts.e: In 1610 he discovered four big moons going around Jupiter.

facts.f: Pure water hardly conducts electricity.
facts.e: Tap water conducts because of the salts dissolved in it. That is why wet hands and switches are dangerous.

facts.f: Ronald Ross showed that mosquitoes spread malaria.
facts.e: He did this work in India and won the Nobel Prize in 1902.
